newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post 16th record close of year.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post 16th record close of year.

text.p: Toronto stocks roared to their 16th record close of the year on Friday, aided by a surge on Wall Street and stronger golds.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 42.62 points to 6492.10, just a shade above the previous peak for the year. It also set a new all-time high of 6498.52 points late in the session.
"It's just a matter of a significant amount of money chasing few prospects," RBC Dominion Securities investment adviser Ira Katzin said.
About 92 million shares were traded worth C$1.43 billion ($1.03 billion).

In New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average leapt 130 points as investors cheered a mixed bag of May U.S. employment data, convinced that they showed the economy growing without inflation, analysts said.
Canada's bond market also rallied. The 30-year benchmark bond closed C$1.94 higher at C$114.32 to yield 6.867 percent.
Twelve of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes ended stronger, led by conglomerates, golds, consumer products and transportation.
There were slight losses in forestry products and real estate. Advancing issues soared past decliners 586 to 359, while 311 stocks closed unchanged.
Toronto edged higher on the week, adding 89 points from the opening on Monday.

Merger mania dominated the oil patch on Friday. CS Resources Ltd. jumped 3.70 to 15 in active trading after Gulf Canada Resources said it planned to offer C$413 million for CS Resources. Gulf shares fell 0.45 to 11.90.

Gandalf Technologies lost 0.97 to 1.63 in heavy trading. The computer network equipment maker said late on Thursday it was almost out of money and was mulling several offers for its undervalued business.
Shares in Canada's largest airline, Air Canada, topped actives, rising 0.50 to 9.25 on more than 2.8 million shares.
